decisive_items: multifocal basophilic foci located predominantly in the perilobular region
polygonal to short spindle-shaped cells formed small nests and sheets within dilated sinusoids without encapsulation
reticular fibers forming a loosely connected, irregular network within tumor cell aggregates
response.rationale: A primitive malignant hepatic tumor in a very young rat with perilobular basophilic foci, spindle/polygonal cells, vascular invasion, and an intratumoral reticulin network is most consistent with embryonal sarcoma. Hepatoblastoma is the nearest age-related differential but is less supported by the spindle-cell morphology and reticulin-rich aggregates; HCC and vascular sarcomas are poor fits for the age and pattern.

rejected.why: Benign lesion with no primitive malignant cells, invasion, or reticulin network.
No glandular/ductal differentiation or desmoplasia; sinusoidal basophilic primitive cells are not cholangiocarcinoma.
Vascular morphology not supported; polygonal cells with clear borders and high N:C contradict hemangiosarcoma.
Generic non-neoplastic label ignores the malignant neoplastic histology and invasion.
Benign adenoma contrad by local vascular invasion and high-grade cytology.
Merely neoplasm; less specific than embryonal sarcoma though malignancy is supported.
Hepatic angiosarcoma less consistent with polygonal nests, clear cell borders, and intratumoral reticulin network.
No supporting evidence; hyperplasia contrad by invasion and frequent mitoses.
HCC is unlikely at this young age and lacks the sarcomatoid/spindle morphology and reticulin-rich aggregate pattern described.
